Jasmine / team / Alice,

Thanks for the clear ask — below is an explicit unpacking so Alice has a single-page answer and two scenarios. I kept the math conservative and included the conversion assumptions so you can change them easily.

Definitions / assumptions we used- Tokens: model tokenizer units (approx 4 characters per token for English on average; varies by language and punctuation).
- Requests: each API call. Billed tokens = tokens the model processes (input tokens + output tokens) for that call when a model executes.
- Prompt caching: if a prefix (system prompt + static ticket metadata) is cached and the cached entry is reused without re-executing the model for that prefix, you do not pay input tokens for that cached prefix on that request. You are billed only for the tokens that the model actually processes. If the response is served entirely from a cache layer without running the model, we bill a small retrieval/serving fee (platform retrieval unit) instead of full model tokens — in our typical commercial scenarios that fee is negligible compared to model execution but we include it in the optimized scenario.

Alice's numbers (from thread)- Monthly characters: 1.2 billion chars/month- API calls: 6,000,000 requests/month- Average user input: 600 chars/request (~150 tokens when dividing by 4 chars/token)- Average model output: 50 tokens/request

Token math (baseline, no caching)- Input tokens/month: 1.2B chars / 4 = 300M tokens- Output tokens/month: 6M requests * 50 tokens = 300M tokens- Total billed tokens/month (baseline): ~600M tokens

Scenario A — Conservative (0% caching, standard usage)- Unit price: $25 per 1M tokens (conservative list-rate proxy)- Monthly cost: 600M / 1M * $25 = $15,000

Scenario B — Optimized (40% cache hit on input prefixes, some fully-cached responses)- Cache assumptions: 40% of requests avoid re-sending a ~150-token input prefix; 5% of requests are entirely served from cache (small retrieval fee = $0.50 per 1k retrievals in our model).
- Effective billed tokens after cache:
  - Input tokens avoided: 300M * 40% = 120M tokens saved
  - New billed tokens = 600M - 120M = 480M tokens (plus retrieval fees)
- Unit price: $12 per 1M tokens (optimized reserved/commit pricing)
- Token cost: 480M / 1M * $12 = $5,760
- Retrieval fees (5% of 6M = 300k retrievals): 300k / 1k * $0.50 = $150
- Total optimized monthly: ~$5,910

Recommended positioning for the customer- Present both scenarios to leadership: Conservative = ~$15k/mo; Optimized = ~$6k/mo (with the caching/commit assumptions).
- For a single easy ask: recommend they target a committed price of $12–15 per 1M tokens for an initial 3–6 month pilot with a commitment band that gives us visibility to tune caching and batching. That maps cleanly into their budget band ($10k–$25k).

Next steps (concrete)
1) Jasmine: send Alice the two scenario lines (I recommend we put the math into pricing-model-scenarios.csv and include both scenarios).
2) Alice: confirm whether you want us to model a separate scenario with heavier outputs (if responses jump from 50 to 200 tokens on average).
3) If they like the optimized scenario, we can propose a 3-month pilot PO with a commitment and a cache-tuning plan (we'll include a simple SLA).

Notes on transparency: all of the above numbers are illustrative and depend on tokenizer details and language distribution. If you want exact token counts we can run their sample text through our tokenizer and provide a line-by-line tokenized export.
